rounds.text: Supreme Facility Management Ltd is trading at a deeply discounted valuation, with a price-to-earnings ratio of just 6.05x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 0.63x [E2], representing a massive discount to sector benchmarks where the P/E sits at 44.61x and P/B at 2.57x [E6, E7]. This statistical cheapness is paired with robust fundamental momentum, demonstrated by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 23% [E12] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 31% [E31], comfortably outpacing sector medians of 12.4% for sales and 12.9% for profit growth [E58, E59]. Furthermore, operating cash flow reached Rs 17 Cr in March 2026 [E27] with strong cash conversion of 2.83x ensuring profits are fully backed by actual cash [E26], while domestic institutional investors have increased their holdings by 3.89 percentage points [E36] to drive positive institutional money flow [E37] within a supportive services sector tailwind [E56]. Conceded: debt exceeds net worth at 1.33x [E30], borrowings rose to Rs 120 Cr [E32], and the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4].

Conceded: the P/E ratio is 6.05x [E1] and the P/B ratio is 0.63x [E2]. However, this statistical cheapness masks severe capital allocation and leverage risks, as evidenced by a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.33x where debt exceeds net worth [E30]. Conceded: 5-year sales and profit growth stand at 23% and 31% [E12, E31], yet the market is heavily discounting this expansion because borrowings climbed to Rs 120 Cr [E32], free cash flow collapsed to Rs -14 Cr [E28], and earnings growth is explicitly flagged as decelerating [E55]. Furthermore, the bull's emphasis on cash conversion of 2.83x [E26] ignores the negative free cash flow reality [E28] and official warnings regarding a low interest coverage ratio [E47] alongside a low return on equity of 10.48% [E8]. Finally, while domestic institutions increased holdings [E36], foreign institutional investors completely abandoned the stock down to 0.00% [E35], and the share price dropped 38% over the past year [E18] while operating margins remain inconsistent [E24].
